gloss: No alternatives; to have no choice.
teaser: Today, we explore a phrase that captures the essence of resignation.
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Today, we explore a phrase that captures the essence of resignation. [break 1s] The phrase is: 无可奈何, wú kě nài hé. [break 1s] 无 (wú) - no; [break 0.5s] 可 (kě) - can; [break 0.5s] 奈 (nài) - to do; [break 0.5s] 何 (hé) - what. [break 1s] So, the full idiom again is: 无可奈何, which literally means 'no way to do anything' and figuratively conveys a sense of helplessness. [break 1s] Here’s the story behind it: [break 1.5s] This idiom originates from a poem in ancient China, where a person finds themselves in an unfortunate situation with no options left. The phrase reflects feelings of powerlessness, as one might face circumstances beyond their control. Over time, it evolved into a commonly used expression when faced with unavoidable difficulties. [break 1.5s] Example one: 我们已经尽力了，结果还是失败了，真是无可奈何。 [break 1s] We did our best, but still failed; it's truly a helpless situation. [break 1s] Example two: 她的病情很严重，我们无可奈何。 [break 1s] Her condition is serious, and we have no choice. [break 1s] Example three: 面对这样的局势，我感到无可奈何。 [break 1s] Faced with this situation, I feel powerless. [break 1s] So, today we learned about 无可奈何, which means to have no choice. Thank you for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom. [break 1s]
